children.translated_text: Refutation of the Doctrine of Universals (<s>Jātivāda-nirāsa</s>)
In accordance with the <s>Buddhas</s>, according to one's understanding of scripture and tradition,
Setting aside modesty, certain points of debate are written down.

children.text: तत्र तावद्बादो जातिवाद एव निराक्रियते;--इह यद्वस्तुनो
भेदाभेदाभ्यामभिधेयं न भवति तत्सर्वं वस्तु न भवति यथा
children.translated_text: a sky-lotus (<s>vyomakamalam</s>). And the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) cannot be denoted by either difference or non-difference — this is
[cont.]
[cont.]
non-apprehension of the pervader (<s>vyāpakānupalabdhi</s>). Now, this
is not an unestablished reason (<s>hetu</s>). For one cannot denote the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) as either different from or identical to
the particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>). In either case, the consequence would be
that it lacks the nature of a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>). For thus: if the universal is held to be

children.text: र्थान्तरमेव सामान्यमभिमतं वस्तु; तदा न तत् तासां सामान्यं
children.translated_text: an entity entirely distinct from the particulars, then it would not be their universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)

children.text: नाम । यत्खलु यतोऽर्थान्तरं न तत् तस्य सामान्यम्, यथा
children.translated_text: at all. For whatever is distinct from something is not its universal — just as
a horse is not the universal of a cow. And cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>) is indeed distinct — this constitutes the apprehension of contradictory concomitance (<s>viruddha-vyāpty-upalabdhi</s>).

Among these, first the debate known as the doctrine of universals (<s>jātivāda</s>) is refuted: Here, whatever cannot be denoted by either difference or non-difference from a thing, all that is not a real thing — just as

children.text: ननु च व्यक्तिभ्योऽर्थान्तरं च स्यात् सामान्यं च
तासामिति न विरोधं पश्यामः । न चैतन्मन्तव्यमर्थान्तरं
children.translated_text: — we see no contradiction. And one should not think: 'If it is distinct,
[cont.]

children.text: दर्थान्तरस्य सामान्यम्, सर्वं सर्वस्य सामान्यं स्यात्
children.translated_text: then it would be the universal of anything distinct, and everything would be the universal of everything else,'

children.text: विशेषाभावादिति । यद्धि खल्वेकं वस्त्वनेकत्र समवेतं तत्तदीयं
children.translated_text: due to the absence of a distinguishing feature. For indeed, whatever single entity inheres (<s>samaveta</s>) in many things is their universal. And since a horse does not inhere in cows, how could it be the universal of cows

children.text: सामान्यम् । गोषु चाश्वो न समवेत इति कथमसौ गवां
children.translated_text: [cont.]
[cont.]
So where is the absence of a distinguishing feature? This is an inconclusive (<s>anaikāntika</s>)
reason — how can it suffice to establish what is desired?
If you say so, that too
follows the prattle of a child. For the distinguishing feature must be stated by an intelligent person —
one that, being present solely in the category of the universal, would establish an orderly distinction without confusion.
But this multiple inherence (<s>aneka-samavāya</s>) exists also in composite substances and effects such as number (<s>saṅkhyā</s>), conjunction (<s>saṃyoga</s>), and so forth,
and therefore those too would be universals of the things possessing number and the like.
Now you might think: Even though there is inherence in many things, only that which is
the cause of identical cognition and designation (<s>samāna-jñāna-abhidhāna</s>) is the universal, and nothing else. 'The state of being
common' (<s>samānānāṃ bhāvaḥ</s>) is universality (<s>sāmānya</s>) —
the meaning is: designation and cognition arise from this [common nature] of yours.
As <s>Akṣapāda</s> states

children.text: इति वात्स्यायनभाष्यं तद्वार्तिकं तट्टीकां च पर्यालोच्य नैयायिकाभिप्रायपूरणेनानुवदति;--समानज्ञानाभिधानप्रसवात्मिका जातिः । इति

children.translated_text: "<s>Jāti</s> (universal) is that whose essence is the production of identical cognition and designation."
This too merely illuminates one's own procedure.
For thus — here

children.text: विकल्पद्वयमुदयते । किं ते भेदाः स्वरूपेण समानाः स्वहेतो
children.translated_text: a twofold alternative arises: Are those particulars (<s>bhedas</s>) identical in their own nature, produced from their own causes, such that the universal in them is the basis for such cognition and designation?
[cont.]

children.text: आहो स्विदसमाना एवेति ? तत्र ते यदि
children.translated_text: Or are they in fact not identical? In that case, if they are
identical by their own nature,

children.text: समानज्ञानाभिधानं स्वयमेव प्रवर्तयिष्यन्ति; किं तत्र सामान्ये
children.translated_text: they will themselves produce identical cognition and designation; what need then for a universal (<s>sāmānya</s>)

children.text: नार्थान्तरेण ? तथा च तदसामान्यमेव । तद्वलेन सामान्येन
children.translated_text: as a separate entity? And thus it would not be a universal at all, since cognition and designation would not be produced by force of that universal.

children.text: ज्ञानाभिधानयोरप्रयुक्तेः । अथासमानाः, न तर्हि तेषां सामान्य
children.translated_text: But if they are not identical, then they would have no universal.
You have said: 'The state of being common is universality.' One who says 'the state of being uncommon is universality' —

children.text: भावः सामान्यमिति ब्रुवाणः कथं श्लाघनीयप्रतिज्ञो देवानांप्रियः ?
children.translated_text: how can such a 'dear fool' (<s>devānāṃpriya</s>) be worthy of praise for his thesis?

children.text: स्वयमसमानभावा अपि तेनैव समानास्त इति चेत्; न; तथा
children.translated_text: If you say: though not identical in their own nature, they are made identical by that very [universal] — no; for

children.text: हि--किं ते क्रियन्ते ? किं नु वै व्यवसीयन्ते ? तत्र न तावत्क्रि
children.translated_text: thus: Are they made so? Or are they merely cognized as such? They are not made so,

children.text: यन्ते, तेषां स्वहेतुभिरेव कृतत्वात् । कृतस्य च पुनः करणायो
children.translated_text: since they have already been produced by their own causes. And there is no occasion for producing again what is already produced,
since production is characterized by the origination of what did not previously exist.
If you say they are made identical in nature —

children.text: क्रियन्त इति चेत्, ननु येषां निष्पन्नतया कृतेः कर्मता नास्ति
children.translated_text: but for those whose production is complete and which therefore cannot be objects of making, how can they be said to be 'made'?

children.text: कथं ते क्रियन्ते नाम ? स्यादेतत्;--येन धर्मिरूपेण ते निष्पन्नाः
children.translated_text: One might say: In the aspect in which they are already produced as particular entities (<s>dharmin</s>),

children.text: न तेन करोतेः कर्मभावमनुभवन्ति; किं तु समानेन पुना
children.translated_text: they do not undergo the status of being objects of making; but in a common aspect in which they are not yet produced,

children.text: रूपेणानिष्पन्नाः क्रियन्ते इति न किञ्चिदनुपपन्नम् । एवं तर्हि
children.translated_text: they are made — and there is nothing inconsistent in this. In that case, then,

children.text: तदेव समानं रूपं सामान्येन क्रियन्त इति स्यात् । तस्य च
children.translated_text: it would follow that that very common form is what is made by the universal. And
for that [common form], which will come into being later — being unproduced and arising subsequently from another cause —
its nature as something existing in particulars (<s>vyaktivad-bhāva-svabhāvatā</s>) cannot be established even by <s>Brahmā</s>
himself.

children.text: न्तरमेव तद्भवतु न किञ्चिदनिष्टमापद्यत इति चेत्; सामान्यान्तर
children.translated_text: If you say: let it be a separate entity, no undesired consequence follows — then it would be

children.text: मेव तर्हि तन्नित्यसामान्यजन्यमभ्युपेतं स्यात् । तथा च भेदानां
children.translated_text: merely another universal, produced by the eternal universal, and so accepted. And then, how can there be a universal of particulars
that are not identical? — when even upon accepting the creation of a universal-form distinct from those [particulars],
an infinite regress (<s>anavasthāna</s>) arises in the form of imagining successive higher and lower effect-universals,
which remains without remedy. Nor would the non-different [particulars] lose their dissimilar form. Nor is
[cont.]
resorting to the second alternative preferable. For things that are different are not cognized

children.text: समाना नाम प्रतीयन्ते । तद्वदन्ये नाम प्रतीयेरन् । भूतवत् ।
children.translated_text: as identical through another [entity]; they would rather be cognized as different — like a ghost (<s>bhūta</s>).

children.text: कथं ? गुणेन; अन्यथा हि येन केनचिदन्येन ये केचन समानाः
children.translated_text: How so? Through a quality (<s>guṇa</s>); for otherwise, any things whatsoever would be cognized as identical with any other thing whatsoever,
[cont.]
since there is no fixed restriction. If you say: because a single entity inhering in many things

children.text: नार्थेन अन्ये समानाः प्रतीयन्ते ततो नातिप्रसङ्ग इति चेत्,
children.translated_text: is the basis for cognizing others as identical, there is no overextension —
that is mere talk. For even the numbers such as duality (<s>dvitva</s>) of small composite substances

children.text: नेकसमवायिद्वित्वे न स्तः । येन तेभ्योऽवयवादयो न तथा
children.translated_text: do not lack being both one and inhering in many. Therefore, parts and the like should also be cognized
in the same way from them. If you say this fault does not apply because they lack the capacity to produce identical cognition and designation
in their substrata — but the universal too was postulated in the particulars precisely because of being one and inhering in many,

children.text: याभ्यामेव समानप्रत्ययहेतुतया परिकल्पितम् । अथ ते च
children.translated_text: as the cause of identical cognition. And those [properties of being one and inhering in many]
are admitted by you for composite substances and the like as well — so how can their having the same status
be denied? If you say: because they do not have the nature of universals, they are not valid reasons for inference —

children.text: इति चेत् । ननु समानज्ञानहेतुत्वे सति सामान्यस्वभावता;
children.translated_text: but having the nature of a universal consists in being the cause of identical cognition,
and being the cause of identical cognition depends on having the nature of a universal — this is clearly mutual
dependence (<s>itaretarāśrayatva</s>). For thus: when asked why oneness (<s>ekatva</s>) and the like, being causes [of identical cognition] just as the admitted universal is,
should not also have the nature of universals — as do composite substances and the like —
you have answered: 'Because they produce identical cognition.' Then that very
property of being the cause of identical cognition, since the cause is equally present,

children.text: यव्यादेरपि किं न स्यादिति अस्मदीयेषु पुनः पर्यनुयोगे
children.translated_text: why should it not also belong to composite substances and the like? — and when we press this question again,
you who say 'because they do not have the form of universals' — how do you escape the fault of mutual
dependence (<s>itaretarāśraya</s>)?
Objection: The universal (<s>sāmānya</s>) could be both distinct from the particulars and yet be their universal
: 'Cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>) does not [exist] in a cow [prior to the universal],

children.text: येन गोत्वयोगात् प्राग्गौरेवासाविति व्यर्थं गोत्वं स्यात् । अपि
children.translated_text: such that, because of the connection with cow-ness, it was already a cow before that — which would make cow-ness pointless. Rather,

children.text: तु यदैव वस्तु तदैव गोत्वेन सम्बद्ध्यते । न च गोत्वयोगात्
children.translated_text: the very moment the entity exists, it is connected with cow-ness. And there is no entity

children.text: प्राग्वस्त्वस्ति । न चाविद्यमानं गौरित्यगौरिति वा शक्यं व्यपदेष्टु
children.translated_text: prior to the connection with cow-ness. And what does not exist cannot be designated as either "cow" or "non-cow."'

children.text: मिति । तथा हि;--यदैव वस्तु तदैव यदि गोरूपं तत्स्वहेतो
children.translated_text: For thus: if at the very moment the entity exists it has the cow-form, produced from its own cause,

children.text: रुत्पन्नं किं तस्यान्येन गोत्वेन ? अथ अगोरूपं, न तर्हि तस्या
children.translated_text: what need has it for another cow-ness (<s>gotva</s>)? But if it lacks the cow-form, then for that [entity]

children.text: गोरितिवाऽश्वादेरिति वा गोत्वेन सह सम्बन्धः स्यात् । न
children.translated_text: there could be no connection with cow-ness — neither as 'cow' nor as 'horse' and so forth.

children.text: ह्यगोभावो गोत्वं नाम! तस्मात् नार्थान्तरं सामान्यमिति ।
children.translated_text: For non-cow-nature is certainly not cow-ness! Therefore, the universal is not a separate entity.
Being a separate entity is pervaded by lacking the nature of a universal — this repudiates

children.text: यति, कुतोऽनेकान्तः ? अभिन्नमेव तर्हि सामान्यमस्तीति व्यक्ति
children.translated_text: universality itself. So how can there be inconclusiveness (<s>anaikāntika</s>)? Then the universal is simply non-different [from particulars] — thus, since a universal separate from particulars
has been refuted.
By this, the following statement of <s>Uddyotakara</s> is also answered

children.text: दत्तसहायकः साङ्ख्य इदानीं प्रत्यवतिष्टंते; स एवं
वक्तव्यः; किं नु वै भवान् व्यक्तीनां सामान्यसंज्ञाकरण
children.translated_text: Do you wish merely to apply the designation 'universal' to the particulars (<s>vyaktis</s>)?

children.text: कामः ? यद्वा, आत्मातिशयप्रतिपादनकामः ? आद्ये पक्षे न
children.translated_text: Or do you wish to demonstrate a superiority of the self (<s>ātman</s>)? In the first alternative,

children.text: किञ्चित् क्षीयते; न वयं नाम्नि विवदामहे । द्वितीयोऽपि पक्षो
children.translated_text: nothing is lost — we do not quarrel over names. The second alternative too
reveals a great wealth of wishful thinking. For thus: here too a twofold

children.text: द्वयमुदयते, किं व्यक्तिभ्यः सामान्यस्याभेदः ? उत व्यक्तीनां
children.translated_text: alternative arises — is the universal non-different from the particulars? Or are the particulars non-different
from the universal? In the first alternative, the universal would be, like the particulars, multiple and non-eternal.
The argument: whatever is non-different from the particulars is

children.text: कमनित्यं च, यथा तासां प्रातिस्विकं रूपम् । व्यक्तिभ्यस्त्व
children.translated_text: multiple and non-permanent, like their individual forms. And the universal is

children.text: भिन्नं सामान्यमिति स्वभावहेतुः प्रसङ्गः । नानैकान्तिको हेतुः,
children.translated_text: non-different from the particulars — this is a natural-reason argument (<s>svabhāva-hetu prasaṅga</s>). The reason is not inconclusive,
since through the superimposition of contradictory properties — oneness and eternality — upon the universal, its difference from the particulars

children.text: सुखादिभ्य इव अन्यस्य एकान्तेन भेदभङ्गात् । अपरस्मिन्
children.translated_text: is definitively established, just as [the self is different] from pleasure and the like. In the other
alternative, the particulars too, like the universal, would be one and eternal.

children.text: प्रयोगःः--यत्सामान्यादभिन्नं न तद्भिन्नमनित्यं च; यथा तस्यैव
children.translated_text: The argument: whatever is non-different from the universal is not multiple and not non-eternal; just as

children.text: सामान्यता; सामान्यादभिन्नं च व्यक्तीनां रूपमिति व्यापक
children.translated_text: the universality of that [universal] itself. And the form of the particulars is non-different from the universal — this is an apprehension of what contradicts the pervader
(<s>vyāpaka-viruddha-upalabdhi prasaṅga</s>). Nor is it inconclusive, for what is non-different from the universal

children.text: हि सामान्यमेव । तच्चैकं नित्यं चेत्, कथं तदभिन्नं भिन्नम
children.translated_text: is the universal itself. And if that is one and eternal, how can what is non-different from it be called multiple

children.text: नित्यं च नाम ? एवं ब्रुवाणः सामान्यमेवानेकमनित्यं च ब्रूयात् ।
children.translated_text: and non-eternal? One who speaks thus would be saying that the universal itself is multiple and non-eternal.

children.text: तस्य च साक्षादभिन्नत्वनित्यत्वे प्रतिज्ञाय पुनरयं देशान्तरत
children.translated_text: Having first asserted that [the universal] is directly non-different and eternal, and then saying 'it appears differently in different locations' —
how is he not a madman? Therefore, it is established that the universal (<s>sāmānya</s>), being inexpressible by either difference or non-difference,
[does not exist as claimed].
Now the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> philosopher, having been given assistance [by the preceding argument], takes a stand. He should be addressed thus:

children.text: न चायमनैकान्तिको हेतुः । यद्यपि हि सामान्यं भेदाभेदा
व्यक्तय एव आभ्यां केवलाभ्यामवाच्यम्, तथापि प्रकारान्तर
children.translated_text: the particulars alone being inexpressible by these two taken separately — nevertheless, a third possibility
exists, namely having the nature of both. For the <s>Jainas</s> maintain that the universal is precisely both different and non-different,
and thus. As they say:
"With respect to the destruction, origination, and persistence of pot, clay, and gold,
people experience grief, joy, and indifference, each with good reason."
"The manifest (<s>vyakta</s>) does not arise from the universal aspect nor does it perish, due to continuity;
it perishes and arises through the particular aspect, being existent through simultaneous arising and so forth."
Just as

children.text: यदा तु शबलं वस्तु युगपत् प्रतिपद्यते ।
मत्तोन्मत्तेतरः प्रतिपद्येत ? तथा हि,--तन्नाम तस्मादभिन्नं यदेव
यत्; भिन्नं च तत्तस्माद्यद्यन्न भवति । अतश्च व्यक्तिभ्यस्सा
मान्यं भिन्नमभिन्नं चेति ब्रुवाणो व्यक्तयस्सामान्यं न व्यक्तिभ्यः
प्रयोगः--यद्यदेव न तत् अतद्भवति यथोष्णं वह्निरूपं नामो
प्रसङ्गः । उभयथा प्रतीतेरुभयोपगम इति चेत् । ननु, प्रतीति
रप्रतीतेर्वाधिका न तु मिथ्याप्रतीतेः वितथस्यापि प्रतीति
दर्शनात् । अन्यथा हि प्रतीतिपथानुसारिणा भवता द्विचन्द्रा
दयोऽपि न निह्नोतव्याः । बाधकवशात्ते निह्नूयन्ते इति चेत्;
पश्यति देवानांप्रियः ? न संविदो युक्तिभिरस्ति बाधेति चेत्;
ननु किमियं राज्ञामाज्ञा येनाविचार्य गृह्येत । प्रत्यक्षस्वभावा
संवित् तच्च ज्येष्ठं प्रमाणमतो न बाध्यत इति चेत् । किं पुनरनु
मानं लक्षणोपेतमपि बाध्यते ? एवमेतदिति चेत् । न तर्हि
पुनरियं संवित्तिः तत्कथमिति बाध्यत इति चेत्; नन्वियमपि
प्रत्यक्षस्य तदाभासतां बाधकत्वात् साधयति न त्वनुमान
प्रत्यक्षायाः प्रत्यक्षाभासता व्यवस्थाप्येत ? न खलु ज्वाला
दीनां क्षणिकत्वं साधयत् बाधकमेव तस्या इत्यकामेनापि तु
कुमारिलेनाभ्युपेतव्यम् । न च शक्यं वक्तुं सामान्यमेव केवलं
तथा विषयीक्रियत इति! तथा हि तदेवेदं ज्वालात्वमिति
स्यात् न सैवेयं ज्वालेंति । तस्मान्नानैकान्तिको हेतुरित्यलं

children.text: उत्पादव्ययधर्मकाः पर्यायाः । यथा सत्यपि द्रव्ये जायमाना
व्ययमानाश्च केयूरादयः । यथा घटं भञ्जयित्वा मौलिः क्रियते
तथा घटो नश्यति मौलिरुत्पद्यते, सुवर्णं तु नोदेति न व्येति,
न नाशेन विना शोको नोत्पादेन विना सुखम् ।
स्थित्या विना न माध्यस्थ्यं तस्माद्वस्तु त्रयात्मकम् ॥
न्तिको भेदो अभेदो वा अभ्युपगम्यते, किं तु देशकालस्व
वर्ण्यते । न हि कटकादीनामन्यो देशोऽन्यं एव सुवर्णस्य च!
न च कटकादयः सुवर्णाद्भिन्नकालाः! नापि कटकादीनां
सुवर्णस्य च स्वभावे नानात्वमस्ति! अतो देशकालस्वभावा
नामेकत्वादेकता द्रव्यपर्याययोः । एकं द्रव्यं बहवः पर्याया इति
पर्यायाः इति लक्षणभेदः । केयूरकटकाभ्यां च कफोणि पाणि
भूषणं क्रियते, सुवर्णेन तु केयूरादिकं तदेवेति कार्यमपि भिद्यते
अत्रैवं चिन्त्यते; यदि तावत् द्रव्यपर्याययोः स्वभावा
न हि ययोः स्वभावाभेदः तयोरन्यथा पारमार्थिको भेदः
सम्भवी । भेदे च तयोरभिधीयमाने स्वभावभेद एव तयोरभ्यु
पगतो भवेदिति न तयोः स्वभावाभेदेनाभेदः सिध्येत् । नच
तेनैव स्वभावेन भेदश्चाभेदश्च । नचान्येन स्वाभावेन भेदोऽन्येना
वस्तु तयोरन्ये एव चान्योन्यभिन्ना द्रव्यपर्याया इति नैकमने
कात्मकं वस्तु वस्तुतः समर्थितं स्यात् । स्वभावेन चाभेदे
स्वभावेन भेदो न तयोर्देशकालाभेदादप्यभेदो यथा रूपरसयोः ।
यदि च पर्यायाणां द्रव्यस्वभावेनाभेदः, तदा पर्यायाणां द्रव्यात्म
संख्याबाहुल्यं नास्तीति पर्याया इति बहुवचनं न प्राप्नोति ।
संज्ञिभेदाभावाच्च न तदांश्रयः संज्ञाभेदः । अथ पर्यायेभ्यो
ययोरेकत्वे सत्यनुवर्तते द्रव्यं तदात्मकं च पर्यायं रूपं व्यावर्तत
अप्यनुवर्तेरन् । अन्यथा हि तदेवानुवर्तते नानुवर्तते चेति स्यात् ।
पर्यायेभ्यश्च द्रव्यस्याभेदे तेषु व्यावर्तमानेषु द्रव्यमपि व्यावर्तेत;
अन्यथा हि त एव तथैव व्यावर्तन्ते न व्यावर्तन्ते चेति स्यात् ।
न चैतदनुन्मत्तो ब्रूयात् । स्वभावाभेदं च द्रव्यपर्याययोर्वर्णयता
द्रव्यस्य कार्यं यत्तत् पर्यायजातस्य; यच्च पर्यायजातस्य तद्द्रव्य
दितं भवति । तथा च सति द्रव्यपर्याययोः
कार्यभेदो न सम्भवत्येव प्रागेव तन्निबन्धनो भेदः । एकस्याप्य
मनेकधा कुर्वन्नवलोक्यत इति न कार्यभेदादपि भेदव्यवहारो
सर्वं हि वस्तु रूपेण भिद्यते न परस्परम् ।
इति । यदि हि यदेव वस्तुत्वं तदेव वेदचाण्डालालापयोः
भेद इष्यत इति चेत्; प्रकारान्तरं तद्वतो वस्तुरूपादनर्था

children.text: एव भावाः परस्परव्यावृत्तमूर्तयो न केनचिदंशेन मिश्रा
children.translated_text: entities whatsoever, having forms mutually excluded from one another, are not in any respect mixed
with one another. As it has been said:
'All entities are established in their own respective natures by their own nature,
since they partake of exclusion from both their own nature and other natures.'
Therefore, the doctrine of <s>anekāntavāda</s> (non-absolutism) should not be maintained by the wise.
